prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by proximity-inducing PROTACs and molecular glues

statement.case_for: After reading the openings I have moved B026 up from my fourth place. Three colleagues placed it first and a fourth placed it second, which is the broadest support of any shortlisted candidacy, and the arguments are scientific as well as popular. The chemical principle is clean and can be stated in physical terms: a bifunctional or monovalent molecule induces a ternary complex that brings a target and an E3 ligase into proximity, so that ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation follow. Ternary-complex formation is measurable by kinetics, thermodynamics and structure. The attributable core is compact: the PROTAC concept and proof of principle (Crews and Deshaies, with Sakamoto) and the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target (Handa, with Ito), which explains molecular glue degraders. That gives a three-person prize with a coherent citation covering both modalities. Independent confirmation is extensive, and degraders are in late-stage trials.
statement.case_against: Maturity and attribution are the real weak points. No PROTAC drug is approved yet, so the long-term consequence rests on a trajectory rather than a settled record. The three-person limit forces us to leave out Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structural work), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and the expert reports will need to show that the omissions are defensible. The molecular glue arm and the PROTAC arm are partly distinct achievements, so the citation risks reading as a line of work. Also, my own opening put B028 (Gray, Winkler) first on purely scientific grounds, and its only first-place vote came from me. I do not want opening enthusiasm for a drug-discovery field to displace a mechanism-level contribution without checking it against the reports.

responses.point: B026 is a new pharmacological principle (degrade rather than inhibit), the idea is simple and elegant, and the mechanism is firmly established after more than two decades.
responses.response: I agree on principle and on independent confirmation, and your argument moved me up from fourth. I qualify one point: simplicity of the idea is not the same as clean attribution. Whether Ciulli's VHL ligands and structure-guided ternary-complex work are decisive for the modality is a question the reports have to answer before we settle on Crews, Deshaies and Handa. I also would not count the missing PROTAC approval as irrelevant, since lenalidomide-class glues are approved but the PROTAC arm is still pending.

responses.point: B067 (sequencing by synthesis) turned DNA reading into a massively parallel chemical process whose impact is quantitatively clear, near-universally adopted and arguably overdue, with Balasubramanian and Klenerman as the chemical core.
responses.response: I take B067 seriously and it is more mature than B026, so I will not dismiss it. My reservation is attribution, which you also note: the platform lineages (Solexa, 454 pyrosequencing, others) complicate a two-person prize, and the expert reports would have to establish that the reversible-terminator chemistry, not the platform or instrument engineering, is the attributable discovery. If that holds, B067 is a credible rival, and I would put it above B031 and B039 on the evidence available.

responses.point: B031 reframed intracellular organisation as phase separation, a general physical-chemical principle with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the central names.
responses.response: I sympathise with the physical-chemistry framing, but I disagree that the timing is clearly right. As you note, there is a real dispute about how far in-cell condensates are thermodynamic phase separation, and this is a field defined by a concept applied across many systems rather than one clearly attributable discovery. Pappu and Mittag's theory adds a further attribution problem inside a three-person cap. I would want the reports to say whether the in-vivo evidence has matured before I put B031 ahead of B026.

responses.point: B001 (nitrogenase) rests on determined structures that revealed the FeMo cofactor and its central carbide, though the catalytic mechanism is still debated.
responses.response: We agree on the facts. Structure is mature, mechanism is not, and that is why I rank B001 below B026 despite my interest in cofactor chemistry. A prize for structure alone might not capture what makes nitrogenase important, and the allocation among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe is hard. I keep it as an alternative, not the preferred prize. I also note that you ranked B026 eighth, so I would like to hear your specific objection to it.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat Ciulli's contributions as decisive enough to displace one of Crews, Deshaies or Handa.
Whether PROTAC and molecular glue work are one achievement or two, and whether absence of an approved PROTAC drug counts as prematurity.
Whether B028 (Gray, Winkler) retains enough uncredited scope after Marcus (1992) and the protein electron-transfer contributions of others to be competitive.
Whether the B067 lineage dispute (Solexa versus 454) can be resolved from the reports.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B026 and the other shortlisted candidacies. I am a bioenergetics researcher and a colleague of Xiaodong Zou at Stockholm University, and I would flag B028 and B001 as close to my own field, where my views should be discounted accordingly, but none of the credited names is a known collaborator.
